HD Hyundai makes first sale of its one-ton-payload HDT1000-33 robot

The six-axis arm will load heavy engine blocks into machines and transfer completed parts; initial quantities and contract value remain undisclosed.

RobotsBeat ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

First sale follows development begun in 2024

HD Hyundai Robotics marked the first sale of HDT1000-33 at Hankook R&D in Ansan, South Korea, on November 18. The six-axis arm has a maximum payload of 1,000 kilograms. Development began in February 2024 in response to demand for handling larger and heavier manufacturing components.

Moving and orienting heavy components

The first units are intended to load construction-machinery engine blocks into machining equipment and move completed parts to the next process. Integration must account for gripper weight, the load’s center of gravity and movement clearances. The one-ton rating describes payload capacity, not the robot’s own mass.

Manufacturer figures need application validation

The manufacturer reports positional error within 0.1 millimeters over thousands of movements, without an independent test protocol or full customer-line results. It plans applications in shipbuilding equipment, large vehicle parts and batteries. Initial sales volume and transaction value are not disclosed.
